correctness.rationale: Pongsriiam 2022 Theorem 4.3 explicitly covers every integer >= 93042 in 18B(phi^6). For a contrary representation of 93041, the floor-of-sum inequality restricts the total of positive Beatty indices to 5185 or 5186. The exact Pell identity 2889^2-5(1292)^2=1 gives 0 < (9-4sqrt(5)-18/323)n < 1/323 for 1<=n<=5186. Its complete residue ceiling formula gives a sum of 17 for total 5185, impossible for 18 residues >=1; for total 5186 it gives 18*323-1 and forces seventeen indices divisible by 323 and another congruent to 18 mod 323, so their total >=5509. All estimates are strict where necessary. Integer-square-root checks and finite bitset enumeration independently corroborated arithmetic; they do not prove infinite coverage.

value.rationale: The precise Frobenius number is a natural invariant for the eighteen-fold Beatty sumset whose optimal value was an explicit published conjecture. The parameter m=6 is the first case for which published sharpness was not established. An exact nonmembership proof using a Pell rational approximant resolves the motivated gap, yielding a sharp infinite-coverage threshold. This is a meaningful exact cutoff, not an arbitrary small computation; no broad conjecture or asymptotic all-exponent result is claimed.
